# docs_audit_report — 2026-07-02

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
I would probably close the tab after the Results section. The page starts clearly, then turns into a dense internal scoreboard full of unexplained acronyms, benchmark fragments, and suspiciously perfect metrics without enough links or context to trust them.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradiction — hero says MIT-0, footer says Apache 2.0.
2. Results grid — 12 metric cards with unexplained acronyms and benchmark names.
3. Evidence/trust gap — many strong numbers, but cards do not link directly to artifacts, sample sizes, configs, or confidence intervals.

## DETAILED FINDINGS
### Bloat
- Results section — 12 result cards — cap at 5-6 headline results.
- Writing section — 7 blog cards — cap at 3-4 posts for a landing page.
- Nav bar — 12 text links plus 2 buttons — cap at 5-6 primary destinations.
- Stats bar — 4 stats plus an embedded “Recent progress” result card — too much hero clutter; cap at 3 proof points.
- “Recent progress” hero card — ~70 words — exceeds result-card 60-word cap.
- Preprint paragraph — ~75 words — acceptable by hard cap, but too dense for landing-page proof copy.
- “What you can check” — 7 capability cards — not over the hard cap, but the section becomes a feature dump.

### Internal jargon
- Hero stats — “Verifier AUROC — FoVer math step-errors (5-seed)” — a stranger does not know AUROC, FoVer, or why 5-seed matters.
- Recent progress — “5-seed dual-condition,” “architecture-only,” “Repinned from v2” — reads like lab notebook shorthand.
- Features / APIs — `VerdictRecord`, MCP server, `SessionMemory` — integration jargon without explanation.
- Features / Test-Time Compute — “TTC,” “PREM,” “Process-Reward Energy Model variance,” “intrinsic motivation” — acronym pileup with no landing-page payoff.
- Results — “KV260 FPGA,” “Ising sampler,” “HumanEval-50,” “EstimationVerifier,” “SVAMP,” “FoVer,” “CRANE,” “VeriCoT,” “GSM8K,” “PRM-BiasBench,” “HalluGuard v3,” “CCTU” — most readers cannot evaluate these.
- Writing — “NTK,” “30B,” “self-distillation” — acceptable for blog readers, but hostile to a cold landing-page scan.
- “X/Y criteria met” equivalent — “60/60 attacks” — closeout-style success count without enough context.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Recent progress — “Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit” — internal revision-history language.
- Preprint — “paper-v6,” “landed within the published confidence interval,” “pending operator-initiated upload” — reads like release/process status, not public copy.
- Writing cards — “seven-rule detector we shipped,” “three-layer defense we shipped,” “two retractions, one rescue” — interesting, but the landing page starts sounding like an internal postmortem archive.

### Inconsistencies
- License: “MIT-0 · Open Source” and meta description “MIT-0” vs footer “Apache 2.0 License.”
- Install status: hero says PyPI and HuggingFace are available; preprint says arXiv submission is prepared but pending. That is not contradictory, but it mixes shipped-product status with not-yet-public-paper status in a way that weakens confidence.
- AUROC framing: hero says 0.9131 FoVer AUROC; recent progress says v2 was 0.9857 and architecture-only is 0.8947; results also says “0.91 AUROC” for prompt injection. These may be separate metrics, but the page makes them easy to confuse.
- Code repair: feature card says HumanEval repair adds +3 points; results also claims HumanEval-50 Ising-guided fuzzing improves 66% to 84% (+18pp). These may be different experiments, but a stranger sees conflicting magnitude.

### Missing essentials
- What Carnot does in one sentence: mostly present in the hero, but the H1 is vague and overclaims “total confidence.”
- Why trust the numbers: partially present, but weak. Result cards need direct artifact links, sample sizes, model names, dates, and confidence intervals.
- How to install it: PyPI install is present, but Rust/CLI/API install paths are unclear.
- License: present but contradictory.
- Who maintains it: footer names Ian Blenke, but there is no maintainer section, governance note, or project status owner.

### Fabrication signals
- “1.0” GSM8K extraction TP rate — perfect score without sample size or artifact link.
- “60/60 attacks” caught — perfect result, no attack set definition.
- “0.0pp accuracy delta” — suspiciously exact without confidence bounds.
- “2.0× speedup, identical losses” — too clean without hardware/setup details.
- “99.3% of wrong code flagged” — high precision on 164 HumanEval problems needs denominator and method.
- “30,658 automated tests” and “382 completed milestones” — impressive but reads like vanity telemetry, not user-relevant evidence.
- “Zero false positives” in blog card — classic credibility-risk phrase unless immediately anchored.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The opening “LLMs predict. They don’t check.” section is clear and stranger-friendly.
- The Extract → Check → Repair explanation is the best part of the page: concrete, sequential, and understandable.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
- Resolve the license contradiction immediately.
- Cut the Results grid to a small set of externally legible claims with direct artifact links.
- Remove or explain unexplained acronyms in visible landing-page copy.
- Replace internal process phrases like “paper-v6,” “repinned,” and “operator-initiated upload.”
- Move most blog/process/autonomous-research material off the main landing page.
- Add a compact maintainer/license/install block near the Quick Start.
- For every perfect or near-perfect metric, show denominator, benchmark, model, date, and confidence interval or remove it.
